description: Move active trading-ops skill ownership out of the trading_operator wrapper repo and into Spreads. Repoint the user Codex skill symlink to the Spreads-owned skill, add a Spreads external symlink for TradingAgents as the research AI layer, and update docs/guidance so Spreads is the active ops hub while trading_operator is no longer the place for future work.

close_reason: Moved active trading-ops ownership into Spreads. Copied the trading-ops skill under .agents/skills/trading-ops, repointed /home/ade/.codex/skills/trading-ops to the Spreads-owned skill, added external/TradingAgents symlink to /home/ade/Projects/TradingAgents, updated Spreads AGENTS/current_system_state docs, and changed TradingAgents defaults/deploy env convention to the Spreads symlink path. Keep AGENTS.md behavioral/operational, put domain ownership in docs/current_system_state.md, and keep skills as workflow playbooks instead of architecture manuals.
acceptance_criteria: Root /home/ade/AGENTS.md contains global refactor/naming/work-ledger/validation doctrine; spreads/AGENTS.md points to canonical docs and repo workflow without becoming a domain map; docs/current_system_state.md owns the domain ownership map; repo-local skills point to canonical docs and workflow surfaces without duplicating source-of-truth architecture; validation reports doc/skill checks and no automated tests are added.
close_reason: Updated Ade-wide AGENTS doctrine, Spreads repo/package AGENTS guidance, canonical current_system_state domain ownership map, and repo-local architecture/live-ops skills. Kept AGENTS/skills behavioral and workflow-focused while docs/current_system_state.md owns the domain map. title: Build StorageOpsState and clean Ops dashboard
description: Create the dedicated storage/retention operator model and route. StorageOpsState should be separate from live trading state and cheap by default, using Postgres stats, relation sizes, latest retention log/result, retention schedule, and vacuum warnings without scanning raw quote/event tables on page load.
acceptance_criteria: core/services/ops/storage_ops_state.py or an equivalently named module owns storage health; /internal/storage-ops/state exists; /ops reads TradingOpsState for runtime panels and StorageOpsState for storage panels; default storage state does not run pending-prune counts or raw quote/event scans; any deep count mode is explicit/manual and not part of normal dashboard refresh.

title: Remove old ops CLI names and documentation drift
description: Finish the full removal across shipped operator commands, docs, and repo guidance. The old live-doctor/Finviz-ledger/status/trading naming should not remain as active operator product language.
acceptance_criteria: Operator CLI exposes properly named commands such as spreads ops state and spreads storage state or equally clean names; old live-doctor and Finviz-ledger CLI commands are removed from active docs and command surfaces; docs/current_system_state.md, AGENTS.md guidance, and operator runbooks point to the new state commands; rg for live-doctor/finviz-ledger/getOpsTradingHealth/getOpsStatus has no active product references after intentional historical docs are accounted for; no compatibility stubs remain.

title: Move Today dashboard to TradingOpsState
description: Make /today a thin command-center view over TradingOpsState. Remove the frontend stitching that separately fetches live-doctor, trading health, Finviz ledger, and execution runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: /today calls only the trading ops state endpoint for live trading status; duplicate React Query calls and local stitching logic are removed; the page still shows market state, trading gate, runtime adapter, feed freshness, candidate/decision counts, active intents, positions, close lifecycle, and attention; no storage/retention panels are mixed into the live trading page.

title: Delete old trading ops API surfaces
description: Remove the old internal ops API surface and expose the properly named live trading state route. Delete the live-doctor/status/trading/Finviz-ledger route concepts instead of leaving compatibility wrappers.
acceptance_criteria: /internal/trading-ops/state exists and returns TradingOpsState; /internal/ops/status, /internal/ops/trading, /internal/ops/live-doctor, and /internal/ops/finviz-ledger are removed from the product API; api/routes names match the new architecture; old route handlers are deleted, not preserved as wrappers; frontend API helpers for removed routes are gone.

title: Build TradingOpsState as canonical live trading state
description: Create the single live trading control-room model. TradingOpsState should replace the old live-doctor/trading/status/Finviz-ledger composition with one DB-first builder that reports market session, control mode, scheduler, worker lanes, execution runtime, broker-sync freshness, active trading flows, feed freshness, decisions, intents, attempts, positions, close lifecycle, risk/mark health, and operator attention. Finviz long calls should appear as a trading flow such as momentum_long_calls, not as a vendor-ledger product surface.
acceptance_criteria: core/services/ops/trading_ops_state.py or an equivalently named module owns the live trading state; the builder does not call Alpaca live during dashboard render and uses stored broker-sync/account/position/execution state; active Finviz long-call behavior is represented as a trading flow with clear feed/source metadata; useful old helper logic is moved under proper names; old live-doctor/trading/status/Finviz-ledger builders are not used by the new dashboard path.

title: Replace fragmented ops surfaces with canonical ops state
description: Replace the scattered live-doctor/status/trading/Finviz-ledger operator surfaces with two properly named state models: TradingOpsState for live trading operations and StorageOpsState for storage/retention health. This is a breaking cleanup: remove old product surfaces and redundant builders instead of preserving compatibility layers.
acceptance_criteria: TradingOpsState is the canonical live trading operator model; StorageOpsState is the canonical storage/retention operator model; old live-doctor/status/trading/Finviz-ledger dashboard surfaces are removed rather than wrapped; frontend and CLI operator paths use the new names; live validation proves the running stack still reports trading health clearly.

title: Make position and close lifecycle first-class
description: Rewrite position projection and close management around explicit lifecycle contracts. Close decisions, close intents, close attempts, close fills, and position recalculation should be separate concepts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Position projection derives from filled open attempts and close facts.
- Partial open, open, partial close, and closed semantics are explicit or deliberately replaced.
- Close decisions record reason, policy, quote source, limit source, and decision time.
- One-active-close-per-position is enforced or replaced by an explicit close-order policy.
- Close attempts preserve position linkage and sell-to-close/buy-to-close semantics.
- Live validation proves profit/stop/force-close can create and complete a close without duplicate close exposure.
close_reason: Implemented position/close lifecycle projection and close-decision lineage. Validation: ruff check and py_compile passed for touched Python files; lifecycle helper smoke passed; finviz-ledger --env ade-nucbox-k8-plus reported healthy close lifecycle; live-doctor --env ade-nucbox-k8-plus reported healthy feed/direct/broker/close lifecycle.

title: Rewrite execution attempt lifecycle and reconciliation
description: Rewrite the attempt lifecycle so local queue state, adapter submission, broker order state, fills, uncertainty, stale handling, and reconciliation are explicit. This should be adapter-independent and ready for both direct Alpaca and future Python-native multi-leg orders.
acceptance_criteria:
- Attempts move through explicit local, unknown, working, canceling, partial, terminal, and stale phases.
- submit_unknown reconciles by client order id before any failure cleanup.
- Orders and fills are projected under attempts.
- Attempt refresh updates linked intent state without hiding broker uncertainty.
- Stale queued or working attempts have deterministic operator-visible next actions.
- Live validation proves current direct option/equity attempts still submit and refresh correctly.
notes: Added canonical execution-attempt lifecycle projection for local queue, submit_unknown, working, canceling, partial, stale, and terminal states. Attempt payloads now attach lifecycle_state/phase/next_action/broker_order_state/fill counts; refresh and guard paths sync attempt lifecycle evidence back to linked intents without moving intents backward on uncertainty. Runtime validation: focused ruff, py_compile with temp pycache, projection helper smoke, finviz-ledger JSON smoke, live-doctor JSON smoke, and git diff --check.

title: Make risk and admission first-class
description: Move risk/admission into the lifecycle model before attempt creation. Every live entry path should distinguish selected strategy decisions from admission approvals, blocks, and unknowns. Finviz long calls should not rely only on lane-local caps once they are part of the unified lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria:
- Admission outcomes are explicit: approved, blocked, and unknown.
- Admission records include policy snapshot, metrics, blockers, evidence, and reason codes.
- Approved admissions attach to created attempts.
- Blocked or unknown admissions stop before attempt creation and leave operator-visible reasons.
- Canonical automation and Finviz direct entries use the same admission vocabulary.
- Close validation is either represented as close admission or documented as a separate lifecycle with equivalent reason visibility.
notes: Added normalized admission lifecycle payloads for risk evaluation, direct order validation, account-capacity blocks, and broker rejections. Approved admissions now attach to created attempts and are copied back to dispatched intents; blocked direct option opens raise before attempt creation. Finviz ledger now exposes intent admission state/reason. Validation: ruff check, py_compile with temp pycache, admission helper smoke, git diff --check, and read-only finviz-ledger smoke/render.

title: Rewrite intent dispatch around lifecycle contracts
description: Replace or simplify the current execution-intent dispatch path around the new lifecycle contracts. Preserve semantics, not current implementation details: TTL, claim, revoke, supersession, source-active checks, and dispatch events.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intent creation, claim, expiration, revocation, supersession, and dispatch are lifecycle-contract driven.
- Open intents validate their signal/decision source.
- Close intents validate their position source.
- Reprice replacement creates lineage instead of mutating the old intent.
- Operator surfaces show intent state and reason clearly.
- Live validation shows pending intents dispatch or skip with clear reasons.
notes: Routed execution-intent creation and updates through lifecycle transition contracts. Shared active/terminal intent state sets now come from ExecutionIntentState, dispatch and maintenance normalize state aliases, invalid transitions raise lifecycle errors, and repricing marks replaced intents as superseded with replacement lineage. Validation: focused ruff, py_compile with temp pycache, transition helper smoke, git diff --check, and read-only finviz-ledger smoke.

title: Normalize Finviz direct flow into lifecycle decisions
description: Move Finviz direct trading from a special feed-to-intent lane into the lifecycle model. The Finviz feed should produce signal/decision records with the same skip/block/selected language used by the rest of the trading system. This can rewrite the Finviz flow where cleaner.
acceptance_criteria:
- Finviz candidates produce lifecycle-visible signal/decision records before intents.
- Decision output preserves clear reasons such as timing, spread, budget, option selection, and setup reset.
- Trade selection, caps, timing windows, and option-selection behavior can be cleaned up when useful; deliberate behavior changes are documented in the bead close note.
- At most configured caps are armed; repeat same-day trades remain allowed when setup and budget permit.
- The live ledger/CLI/dashboard show Finviz decisions through the same lifecycle vocabulary as other flows.
- Live validation confirms feed refresh, candidate visibility, skip reasons or selected intents, and no duplicate unintended entries.
notes: Implemented Finviz entry lifecycle normalization in the direct trading path. Each entry decision now gets lifecycle-visible trade_signal/trade_decision records with selected/no_entry/skip/selected_blocked states, selected entry intents carry the lifecycle context in their source payload, and the Finviz ledger exposes lifecycle decision state counts and decision ids. Validation: ruff check and py_compile for touched files; finviz-ledger --json live read succeeded; helper smoke produced no_entry/selected/skip states. Existing persisted direct runs predate this code, so live ledger lifecycle counts populate after the next direct run using the updated workers.

title: Implement lifecycle contracts and typed states
description: Introduce the core Python lifecycle contract module for states, transitions, command/event names, and validation helpers. This can replace current string-set logic where sensible. It does not need to keep old internal state names working unless a name is deliberately retained in the target model.
acceptance_criteria:
- Typed/enumerated states exist for intent, admission, attempt, position, and close lifecycle.
- Transition helpers return structured reasons and reject invalid transitions.
- Current lifecycle names are normalized through the new contracts, intentionally replaced, or removed.
- submit_unknown and stale/uncertain broker submission states are explicit.
- uv run python -m py_compile passes for touched Python files.
- Runtime risk is documented if no live behavior path uses the new module yet.
notes: Implemented packages/core/services/trading_lifecycle.py with typed lifecycle states, current-name normalization, allowed transition maps, structured transition decisions, and require/validate helpers. Added docs/planning/2026-06-03_lifecycle_contracts_module.md documenting runtime risk: no live writer consumes the module yet. Validation: uv run python -m py_compile packages/core/services/trading_lifecycle.py; uv run python import/transition smoke check.

title: Create clean lifecycle storage and projection plan
description: Design and implement the durable storage shape for lifecycle facts and projections. Full rewrite is allowed where cleaner than evolving current JSON-heavy shapes. The goal is to separate facts from projections and avoid carrying legacy payload clutter into the new core.
acceptance_criteria:
- Schema/model changes or new tables represent lifecycle facts cleanly.
- Fact records are separated from operator projections where practical.
- Storage state values use or deliberately map to the lifecycle contract module.
- Old tables can be replaced, dropped, archived, or rebuilt after historical-data handling is documented.
- Migration/cutover notes explain whether existing live data is archived, backfilled, discarded, or reset.
- Operator CLIs are updated to report the new lifecycle shape; they do not need to support old and new schemas at the same time.
- Validation uses schema inspection and runtime smoke checks, not new automated tests.
notes: Implemented target lifecycle storage schema: SQLAlchemy models, Alembic migration 20260603_0042, Alembic metadata import, lifecycle schema CLI, and storage cutover planning doc. Target tables start empty under breaking-rewrite posture; live writers are not cut over yet. Validation: py_compile for touched Python/migration files, spreads lifecycle schema --json, spreads lifecycle schema, alembic heads, metadata inspection for 12 trade_* tables, git diff --check. Formatter attempts with uv run ruff/black were blocked because those tools are not installed in the current uv environment. Metadata inspection surfaced an existing SQLAlchemy warning about legacy cyclic FKs among execution_attempts/execution_intents/portfolio_positions/risk_decisions; not introduced by this bead.

title: Define target trading lifecycle object model
description: Define the clean target object model for the trading lifecycle. Use current Spreads and Nautilus as research inputs, but do not preserve current table names, payload shapes, or service layout by default. Decide the authoritative facts for signal, decision, intent, admission, attempt, order, fill, position, close, and reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A design doc defines target objects, fields, state enums, transitions, and invariants.
- The doc explicitly marks which current fields/tables are kept, replaced, merged, or archived.
- submit_unknown, admission approved/blocked/unknown, intent supersession, one-active-close policy, and position projection semantics are covered.
- The doc includes a cutover stance for historical data: archive/read-only, backfill, discard, or reset for each major object.
- No code changes are required for this bead.
notes: Completed target lifecycle object model in docs/planning/2026-06-03_target_trading_lifecycle_object_model.md. The doc defines target objects, fields, state enums/transitions, invariants, current table replacement stance, submit_unknown handling, admission states, intent supersession, one-active-close policy, position projection semantics, and historical-data cutover posture. No code changes were required for this decision bead.

title: Rebuild Spreads trading lifecycle around clean state machines
description: Rework the Spreads trading core around explicit lifecycle objects and transitions for signals, decisions, intents, attempts, broker facts, positions, and closes. Current Spreads and Nautilus implementations are input, not compatibility constraints. Planned downtime is acceptable, and the work should choose clean replacements over compatibility hacks. The goal is a cleaner Python-native trading lifecycle that can retire Rust bridge dependence for live Spreads flows.
acceptance_criteria:
- Child beads define and implement a clean lifecycle model.
- Direct Finviz flow, canonical automation flow, risk/admission, and close management use the same lifecycle language.
- Broker submission uncertainty, repricing lineage, close lifecycle, and position projection are first-class.
- Operator CLI/API/dashboard surfaces expose the new lifecycle states clearly.
- Compatibility shims and dual-running old/new internals are not introduced unless they are the clean target design.
- Live paper validation proves entry, skip, submit, fill sync, close, reprice/cancel where applicable, and broker reconciliation.
- No automated tests are added unless explicitly requested; validation is through live/runtime smoke checks and shipped CLIs.
close_reason: Completed all lifecycle refactor beads through runtime cutover. Active Spreads flow now uses lifecycle decisions/admission/intents/attempts/positions/closes, Python-native Alpaca adapter, operator lifecycle views, and retired Nautilus runtime surface.

title: Add Finviz gross entry budget and pacing guard
description: The Finviz direct lane currently enforces open-position capacity (max_open_positions) and per-run burst capacity (max_new_positions_per_run), but it does not enforce a gross daily/session entry budget. That means exits free capacity and total same-day entries can exceed what an operator intuitively expects from the open cap. Add separate entry-budget controls without banning legitimate same-day repeat trades.
acceptance_criteria: Finviz direct config supports max_daily_entries or max_session_entries separately from max_open_positions; direct-run decisions include max_daily_entries_reached when the gross budget is hit; operator views show filled entries today, remaining entry budget, open position count, and max open positions as separate numbers; same-symbol repeat trades remain allowed when budget remains and setup reset criteria pass; live validation confirms no new entries after the gross budget is reached while exits/close management continue normally.
close_reason: Implemented max_daily_entries/max_session_entries guard for Finviz direct trading, surfaced session entry budget in ledger/live-doctor/console views, deployed scheduler/runtime/API restart, and live-validated the 2026-06-02 18:02Z direct run created 0 intents with max_daily_entries_reached for all 10 entry candidates at budget 12/10.

title: Surface close lifecycle anomalies in ops views
description: We had to use SQL/logs to distinguish historical close failures from current close health. Add a focused close lifecycle/anomaly surface to the CLI/dashboard so operators can immediately see failed close attempts, pending close attempts, stale reconciliation skips, intent-mismatch rejects, and latest filled close proof by position.
acceptance_criteria: live-doctor or a shipped ops CLI shows recent close attempts by status, latest close failure, active/pending close attempts, stale-reconciliation skip count, and latest filled close per open/closed position; Grafana/dashboard exposes the same focused panel without unrelated system logs; validation uses live paper data and requires no automated tests unless explicitly requested.
close_reason: Implemented close lifecycle summaries across live-doctor, Finviz ledger, positions API, and operator positions dashboard. Live/deployed validation: py_compile, diff check, focused web lint, live finviz-ledger close_status=healthy active=0 pending=0 failed=0 stale=3 mismatch=0, live-doctor close_status=healthy, deployed API routes returned close_lifecycle payloads, and web /positions returned 200.

title: Require fresh Finviz setup before same-symbol re-entry
description: Same-day repeat trades are allowed. The risk is not multiple trades; it is immediately re-entering the same stale setup after an invalidation/stop-style exit without evidence that the symbol has reset. Add a simple re-entry reset guard for the Finviz direct lane: allow another trade in the same symbol when a fresh setup forms, but block stale duplicate re-entry against the same feed/setup state.
acceptance_criteria: A symbol can be traded multiple times in the same day when a new Finviz/direct setup is observed after the prior exit; immediate stale re-entry after stop_loss, stop_multiple, underlying_vwap_recent_low_break, or equivalent invalidation is blocked until reset criteria pass; decision output distinguishes same_symbol_setup_not_reset from normal buy_timing_not_ready/spread_too_wide reasons; live validation shows repeat same-day trades remain possible while stale duplicate re-entry is blocked.
close_reason: Implemented a same-symbol re-entry reset guard for Finviz direct trading. Stale same-day re-entry after invalidation exits now returns same_symbol_setup_not_reset until a newer feed snapshot after the prior close is observed; repeat trades remain allowed after the feed reset. Validation: py_compile and diff check passed; focused runtime smoke covered stale block, fresh allow, and hold-exit allow; deployed by restarting worker-runtime; live direct runs at 2026-06-02T18:04Z and 18:06Z completed cleanly, but today’s max_daily_entries cap masks the live repeat-entry branch.

title: Gate exit manager on fresh broker reconciliation
description: The close guard now prevents bad sell_to_close submissions, but exit-manager can still run in the same minute as broker-sync and briefly evaluate positions before the freshest reconciliation has landed. Add an explicit freshness gate so exit-manager only evaluates close decisions against a current broker-sync snapshot, or skips with a clear non-actionable reason when broker-sync is stale/in-flight.
acceptance_criteria: Exit-manager records the broker-sync snapshot/freshness used for each run; if broker sync is stale or unavailable it skips without evaluating closes; after broker-sync completes it evaluates only currently open matched positions; live validation over multiple market-hour ticks shows no closed-position stale decisions and no failed close attempts.
close_reason: Validated live exit-manager broker-sync gate: latest :45Z runs succeeded after broker_sync, recorded current broker snapshot, evaluated 3 matched open positions, and had failure_count=0.

title: Surface Nautilus lifecycle proof in dashboard/API
description: Expose the same Nautilus lifecycle proof now available in spreads trading CLI through the API/dashboard so live operators can see intent, bridge, broker, fill, session-position, and close-runtime state without shelling into the box.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard/API response includes nautilus_lifecycle for paper/live views; open and close runtime proof is visible by strategy family; missing or legacy direct-close proof is clearly distinguished from full Nautilus proof.
close_reason: Surfaced Nautilus lifecycle proof in the runtime dashboard using the existing /internal/ops/trading nautilus_lifecycle payload. The panel shows bridge state, attempts, full lifecycle count, missing/legacy close proof, proof_by_family, and recent attempts. Also made web dev origins target-aware so the dashboard hydrates on localhost, loopback, and the NUC Tailnet host. Validation: web lint for automations-index/lib/api/next.config, py_compile deployments, diff check, deploy render-env showed SPREADS_WEB_ALLOWED_DEV_ORIGINS=localhost,127.0.0.1,100.111.132.114,ade-nucbox-k8-plus, recreated web/api via docker compose up -d web, deployed backend proxy returned nautilus_lifecycle with 5 families, and Playwright browser smoke on http://127.0.0.1:53000/runtimes rendered Nautilus Lifecycle Proof plus /api/backend/automations, /executions/runtimes, and /internal/ops/trading calls.

title: Design partitioned quote and event storage
description: Plan the durable storage fix for ever-growing raw quote/trade/event data separately from the dashboard refactor. The target is date partitioning for high-volume append-only tables and retention by dropping old partitions instead of large row deletes.
acceptance_criteria: A design doc covers partitioning option_quote_events, option_trade_events, and market-heavy event_log rows; the plan defines partition keys, migration/backfill approach, retention changes, backup/rollback stance, market-hours safety, and live validation; it explicitly keeps dashboard/storage state independent of raw table scans; implementation is deferred to a later bead unless explicitly approved.

title: Cut over lifecycle runtime and retire legacy paths
description: Cut over live paper flows to the new lifecycle runtime and remove or disable legacy paths that should no longer be used. Planned downtime is acceptable. No backwards-compatible internals, dual-write paths, or old-runtime fallback are required.
acceptance_criteria:
- Active Finviz paper flow uses the lifecycle runtime.
- Legacy direct paths that bypass lifecycle decisions are disabled or removed.
- Bridge/Rust-dependent Spreads runtime is disabled or removed after Python-native validation, without preserving a fallback path by default.
- Operator docs and planning docs are updated to reflect the new current state.
- Live validation covers feed, decisions, intents, attempts, fills, positions, closes, reconciliation, logs, and resource health.
close_reason: Cut active config to alpaca_direct, rejected new nautilus runtime declarations, marked Nautilus retired in runtime capabilities, removed active NUC bridge binary declaration, updated docs, restarted NUC services, and validated live health. Validation: config validate, ruff check, py_compile, execution-runtimes, deploy render-env/render-compose, live-doctor, jobs lanes, failed jobs, and finviz-ledger after next interval.

title: Build Python-native Alpaca order adapter
description: Build the Python-native Alpaca adapter for single-leg and multi-leg submission using the new attempt lifecycle. It should support direct long calls first, then verticals and iron condors as the order-list shape is proven. This is the Rust bridge retirement path. The bridge can be used as a reference implementation, but it is not a required fallback.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adapter handles single-leg option open/close through lifecycle attempts.
- Adapter handles multi-leg order-list payloads for defined-risk spreads behind explicit live enablement or an operational kill switch.
- Cancel/replace and close attempts preserve lifecycle lineage.
- Broker order snapshots and fills project under attempts.
- Live paper validation proves order submit, broker accept/reject, fill sync, position sync, and close for tiny size.
- Rust bridge fallback is not required inside this adapter path; keep or remove it based on the cutover decision, not compatibility pressure.
close_reason: Centralized Alpaca submit/snapshot/cancel behavior behind a Python-native order adapter and routed direct equity, single-leg option, queued attempt submit, refresh, cancel, and guard cancel paths through it. Validation: ruff check, py_compile, fake-client adapter smoke, execution-runtimes capability check, live-doctor and trading health against ade-nucbox-k8-plus.

title: Expose lifecycle state in CLI API and dashboard
description: Expose the lifecycle model through the operator surfaces. The goal is for live operators to see the current state and next action for signals, decisions, intents, attempts, positions, closes, and broker reconciliation without SQL/log spelunking.
acceptance_criteria:
- live-doctor or a shipped CLI summarizes lifecycle health and anomalies.
- API/dashboard surfaces show active/pending/stale/unknown/terminal lifecycle counts.
- Finviz ledger or equivalent shows decision-to-intent-to-attempt-to-position lineage.
- Close lifecycle proof is visible per open/closed position.
- Runtime validation confirms views work against live paper data.
close_reason: Exposed lifecycle rollups and next-action fields in Finviz ledger/live-doctor JSON and rendered CLI surfaces. Validation: ruff check, py_compile, git diff --check, live-doctor render against ade-nucbox-k8-plus all passed.

title: Expose Nautilus bridge logs in central observability
description: Expose Nautilus bridge/runtime log output in the central Loki/Grafana stack. Today the Nautilus Docker compose project only contributes backing-service logs, while the active bridge runs as a Spreads subprocess and its stdout/stderr are captured instead of emitted to the central app log surface.
acceptance_criteria: Nautilus bridge subprocess stdout/stderr are emitted as structured app logs without leaking full handoff payloads; central Trading Logs/Grafana view has a clear Nautilus bridge/runtime surface; Loki queries can show bridge events from Spreads workers and future Nautilus app container logs; live validation proves the labels/query return recent bridge evidence or a controlled synthetic bridge log without submitting orders; no automated tests are added unless explicitly requested.
close_reason: Exposed active Nautilus bridge logs in central observability. Spreads now emits bridge submit start/success/failure plus bounded bridge subprocess stdout/stderr as structured JSON with component=nautilus_bridge, log_origin_project=nautilus, and log_origin_service=bridge, while skipping the final success result JSON and avoiding full handoff payload logging. Added Nautilus Bridge And Runtime volume/log panels to the central Trading Logs Grafana dashboard, covering bridge logs currently emitted from Spreads app containers and future project=nautilus app container streams. Documented the current bridge-through-Spreads boundary in nucbox-observability README. Validation: py_compile packages/core/services/execution/nautilus_bridge.py, jq parsed grafana/dashboards/trading-logs.json, git diff --check in both repos, Loki query syntax checks passed, restarted worker-runtime and Grafana, synthetic fake bridge command emitted stdout/stderr without submitting orders, Loki returned 4 component=nautilus_bridge records via the dashboard selector, and Grafana API shows the new Nautilus panels loaded. Live-doctor after worker restart kept scheduler/workers/feed/direct/close/Nautilus bridge healthy with market closed and no open positions; remaining BLOCKED is the pre-existing entries=12/10 daily cap state, with broker sync idle/stale after market close.

title: Live-validate Finviz same-symbol re-entry reset after budget reset
description: After the gross daily entry budget resets on a future market session, live-validate that same_symbol_setup_not_reset appears for stale same-symbol invalidation re-entry and that a later fresh Finviz feed setup can allow a repeat same-day trade when other caps permit.
acceptance_criteria: Live ledger/direct-run evidence shows a stale same-symbol invalidation re-entry blocked with same_symbol_setup_not_reset; a later fresh feed snapshot for the same symbol is allowed to proceed to normal timing/option selection when budget and open caps permit; findings are recorded on this bead or the parent implementation bead.

title: Measure Finviz option selection and fill quality
description: Before making more strategy changes, capture the facts around selected contracts: spread, bid/ask/mid, fill price, slippage, volume/open interest when available, option age, exit reason, and realized outcome. This lets us tune strike/expiry/liquidity rules from our own live paper trail instead of guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Each Finviz direct entry/exit records option-selection metrics and fill-quality metrics in the ledger/read model; daily summary reports selected contract quality, fill slippage, exit reason, and outcome by symbol; the data is visible from a shipped CLI or dashboard; no automated tests are added unless explicitly requested.
close_reason: Added Finviz option-selection and fill-quality metrics to the existing ledger/read model without adding schema or tests. Each summarized attempt now carries option_selection facts from the execution intent payload plus fill_quality derived from limit price, selected quote bid/ask/mid, fill price, fill side, spread capture, limit improvement, midpoint slippage, quote spread, quote age, and estimated notional. Positions now include compact entry/latest-close quality, the ledger summary includes weighted daily quality averages, and details.quality_by_symbol reports selected contracts, entry/exit counts, spread, quote age, entry/exit slippage, DTE/delta/volume/OI where present, exit reasons, and PnL by symbol. Validation: py_compile packages/core/services/ops/finviz.py and packages/core/cli/ops_render.py, git diff --check, live CLI finviz-ledger --env ade-nucbox-k8-plus --json returned healthy with 12 entries, 12 exits, 8 quality_by_symbol rows, populated sample entry/exit option_selection and fill_quality; human CLI renders the Finviz Option Fill Quality table; internal API /internal/ops/finviz-ledger returned the same quality summary. Live-doctor remained operational with scheduler/workers/feed/direct/close healthy, market closed, open positions 0, active intents 0; the only BLOCKED flag is the pre-existing entries=12/10 daily cap state.

title: Automate quote and event retention visibility
description: We already hard-pruned stale quote/event data and have an off-hours VACUUM FULL bead, but quote storage needs continuous visibility and retention so it does not become a periodic emergency. Add operator-visible retention metrics and a scheduled retention path for high-volume quote/event tables.
acceptance_criteria: Ops view shows table sizes, retained date ranges, rows pruned in the latest retention run, and whether VACUUM FULL is pending; scheduled retention runs off the live market path and avoids market-hours heavy locks; live validation records before/after table sizes and confirms market-recorder/feed/direct jobs stay healthy.
close_reason: Added retention status visibility for high-volume quote/trade/event tables through the shipped CLI and internal ops API. Status now reports table sizes, retained ranges, latest retention run/matched/deleted counts, and whether VACUUM FULL is pending, with the off-hours schedule surfaced as 30 22 * * 1-5 and ops log discovery via SPREADS_OPS_LOG_DIR. Live validation: py_compile touched Python files, git diff --check, docker compose config, deploy env render includes SPREADS_OPS_LOG_DIR, one-time ops/retention_prune.sh run wrote logs/ops/retention.log and deleted 0 rows because no stale rows remained, CLI/API retention status returned healthy with option_quote_events ~42,951,460 rows/14.8GB/dead=0, option_trade_events ~252,482 rows/122MB/dead=0, event_log ~2,223,264 rows/8.5GB/dead=0, vacuum_full_pending=false, and live-doctor stayed operational with scheduler/workers/feed/direct/close healthy. Remaining live-doctor BLOCKED is the pre-existing 12/10 daily entry cap usage with market closed and no open positions.

title: Add adaptive option close repricing
description: Current option closes have filled in paper, but a fixed close limit can miss exits in fast/illiquid contracts. Add a small, bounded cancel/replace path for option exits so profit/stop/force-close orders can move toward marketability without creating duplicate close exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Close attempts have an age/TTL and one active close per position; unfilled close orders can be canceled/replaced according to a configured repricing policy; replacement attempts preserve sell_to_close and position_id linkage; ops views show original and replacement orders; live paper validation proves no duplicate close and a successful close/final skip path.

comments.author: ade b
comments.text: Implemented bounded Finviz long-call close repricing behind the existing execution-intent manager. Config: option_exit_rules.repricing enabled with stale_after_seconds=75, max_reprices=3, price_step=0.01, max_concession=0.03. Replacement intents preserve sell_to_close, position_id, original/previous limits, previous_execution_attempt_id, and supersedes_execution_intent_id; finviz-ledger now renders recent close attempts with reprice/limit chain. Validation 2026-06-02: config validate ok; py_compile ok with temp pycache; git diff --check ok; synthetic fake-store smoke moved a close sell limit 1.00 -> 0.99, preserved position_id=position-1 and position_intent=sell_to_close, and exhausted after max_reprices; restarted scheduler, worker-runtime, worker-discovery; live-doctor on ade-nucbox-k8-plus was IDLE/healthy with active close attempts=0 and active intents=0. Remaining: market was closed and there were no open positions, so live broker cancel/replace/fill proof still needs the next stale close order.

title: Run off-hours VACUUM FULL after stale quote prune
description:
We hard-pruned stale raw capture on 2026-06-02, deleting 24,235,545 option_quote_events rows and 4,886,632 raw market event_log rows. Normal VACUUM (ANALYZE) cleared dead tuples, but the Postgres database files still report about 23GB because VACUUM FULL was intentionally skipped during live trading. Run only off-hours if OS-visible disk reclamation is still desired.

Recommended runbook:
1. Confirm market is closed and live-doctor is healthy before maintenance.
2. Pause/stop market-recorder plus runtime/discovery workers or put the stack in maintenance mode so writes will not compete with table rewrites.
3. Run VACUUM FULL (ANALYZE) option_quote_events; then VACUUM FULL (ANALYZE) event_log; from the spreads Postgres container.
4. Check pg_database_size, table sizes, disk usage, and logs.
5. Restart paused services and verify live-doctor, Finviz feed/direct health, broker sync, open positions, and actionable failed jobs.

Avoid running VACUUM FULL during market hours because it takes strong table locks and can block live reads/writes.
acceptance_criteria: VACUUM FULL completed off-hours for option_quote_events and event_log, services restarted, live-doctor healthy, and before/after DB/disk sizes recorded.

title: Port long-vol options strategies
description: Port the long straddle and long strangle strategy family into Nautilus after the close-runtime path proves clean in paper. Keep the implementation aligned with the existing regular-strategy pattern, including future buy/sell equity support, without turning it into a dry-run-only path.
acceptance_criteria: Long straddle and long strangle configs/routing exist as regular strategies; validation allows their option-leg shape separately from vertical spreads; execution intents carry enough metadata for Nautilus open/close lifecycle proof.
